content:
simplify our reply to jas for a BA's perspective: Morning Jas! ☕

Good spot — and it's a bit of both. Content-wise, Assistance is basically the same as Shipping & Returns: email, phone, hours, WhatsApp, the Contact Us link — all region-based text/URLs you'd maintain in Contentful. So your "it's all just URLs, works the same as S&R" read is spot on, and I wouldn't split it out for the content.

The one thing that genuinely has more logic is Start a Chat — that's not a URL, it opens the on-site Inside Chat widget. And that's where it gets interesting:

• Inside Chat is consent-gated (Didomi) — can't fire until consent's granted
• The widget owns its own availability — "not visible if all agents are unavailable / closed" is Inside Chat's rule, not something we build in the accordion
• It's a different squad + later sprint — Inside Chat is Squad B, Sprint 7. It doesn't exist in the build yet, and the site token + Didomi category are still open items on the integration.

So my advice: keep Assistance bundled with Shipping & Returns (as you've got it) for the rendering — but carve the chat trigger out as a small follow-up dependency that rides with the Inside Chat integration in Sprint 7, rather than pulling that forward into our PDP work now. Same move we made peeling consent out of Recently Viewed into SFCC-106.

Practically for the accordion story: render Start a Chat as a Contentful-driven link/control that degrades safely — if the widget's loaded (post-consent) it opens it, if not it does nothing fancy. The full "launch + reflect availability" behaviour gets wired when Inside Chat lands.

Tl;dr — Assistance = same content story as S&R ✅. The chat launch = its own little Sprint 7 dependency, not a reason to split the tab.

And 👍 fully agree on keeping Size & Fit separate — even more so now it's dual-source (SFCC + optional Contentful fallback).

I have everything needed. Here is my research report. ## Summary This is retail-react-app **v10.0.0**. The PDP is **not overridden** in this repo — it runs entirely from the base template. The product-information accordion is a small, self-contained partial in the base package, and the repo already has a working Contentful integration pattern (hooks + typed components + config) that a new PDP accordion could plug into. --- ### 1. PDP page structure **No PDP override exists.** `overrides/app/pages/` contains only: `contentfulPreview/`, `experience/`, `home/`, `my-new-route/`. There is no `product-detail/`. The PDP is served entirely from the base template: - `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/product-detail/index.jsx` (~39 KB, the main page) - `.../product-detail/partials/information-accordion.jsx` (the only partial) - `.../product-detail/index.mock.js`, `index.test.js` Routing confirms this: `overrides/app/routes.tsx` spreads the base routes via `..._routes` and adds no `product-detail` entry, so the PDP route is inherited unchanged. **Composition** (from `index.jsx`): the page fetches product/category data, sets SEO via `Helmet`, then renders (all repo-relative to the base package): - `app/components/product-view` — `ProductView` (gallery, name, price, variation attributes, add-to-cart/wishlist). Wrapped in an `Island` with `hydrateOn="visible"`. - `app/pages/product-detail/partials/information-accordion` — `InformationAccordion`, rendered **right after** `ProductView` (line 808 for a normal product; line 776 for each child of a set/bundle). - `app/components/recommended-products` — `RecommendedProducts` (Einstein "Complete the Set" / "You might also like"), each in its own `Island`. So the accordion is a peer of `ProductView`, taking `product` as its only prop. --- ### 2. Accordion usage **Base product-information accordion:** `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/product-detail/partials/information-accordion.jsx` (121 lines). It imports Chakra `Accordion, AccordionItem, AccordionButton, AccordionPanel, AccordionIcon` from `app/components/shared/ui` and renders a hardcoded `` with **four fixed items**: 1. **"Product Detail"** — renders `product?.longDescription` via `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` 2. **"Size & Fit"** — hardcoded "Coming Soon" 3. **"Reviews"** — "Coming Soon" 4. **"Questions"** — "Coming Soon" Each item is a `

...

` + ``. Items are not data-driven or conditionally rendered — they always render, even when empty. Message IDs follow `product_detail.accordion.button.*` / `product_detail.accordion.message.coming_soon`. **Accordion theming:** `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/theme/components/base/accordion.js` (base styles: `button.paddingLeft: 0`, no hover bg). The overrides theme (`overrides/app/theme/components/`) does **not** currently customize the accordion. **Other accordion in base (not PDP):** `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/nested-accordion/` + `app/theme/components/project/nested-accordion.js` — used for nested category/refinement menus, not product information. **Accordion usage in `overrides/`: none.** A grep for `Accordion` across `overrides/` returned zero matches. --- ### 3. Existing product information / tabs components The only such component is the base `information-accordion.jsx` above. There is **no** Tabs-based product-info component, no `product-information` component, and no "Details & Care" / "Shipping & Returns" / "Materials" component anywhere in `overrides/` or the base PDP. The strings "Details & Care", "Shipping & Returns", "Materials", "Care" do not exist in the base PDP — only "Product Detail", "Size & Fit", "Reviews", "Questions". **The PRD is where the target design lives** — `.docs/prd/pdp.md`: - Line 11 (PRD-008, confirmed): "Key supporting information in expandable accordions: **Details, Size & Fit, Care, Shipping & Free Returns** (region-specific content)". This is the real accordion the story targets — it differs from the base's Reviews/Questions items. - §12 (PRD-009, confirmed), lines 142-146: a separate **"Environmental Qualities / AGEC" accordion**, EU storefronts only (`/en-eu/`, `/fr-eu/`), **data sourced from AP21**, and **only renders when data exists** (no empty accordion). - §11 (lines 130-138): Size guide is a **Measmerize slide-out overlay**, with a **Contentful-managed content type as fallback** per product type — separate from the accordion. - Line 20 / 216: **product copy ownership (description/editorial) is still TBD** — Contentful vs SFCC vs AP21. These are natural seams for splitting the story: (a) refactor base accordion into a data-driven Zimmermann component with the correct item set, (b) Care/region-specific content wiring, (c) EU-only Environmental Qualities accordion (AP21 data, conditional render), (d) Size & Fit / size-guide overlay hookup. --- ### 4. Contentful integration for PDP The repo has a complete, custom Contentful pattern under `overrides/app/`: - **Config:** `overrides/app/config/contentful.ts` — `getContentfulConfig()` pulls `app.contentful` from `getConfig()` (space/env/delivery+preview tokens, sourced from `config/default.js`). Plus `overrides/app/config/contentfulMapping.ts` (+ `.generated.ts`) mapping SFCC site IDs → locales and MRT tiers → Contentful environments. Registered content types are minimal so far: `CONTENT_TYPE_IDS = { shoppableImage }`. - **Hooks:** `overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts` — `useContentfulEntry(entryId, preview)` and `useContentfulEntries(contentType, preview)`. Client-side `fetch` against CDA/CPA with `include=2`, resolves linked assets, `AbortController` cleanup. - **Components:** `overrides/app/components/contentful/` — `heroBanner`, `duplexSection`, `videoEmbed`, `productHero`, plus `experiences/` (Studio Experiences: `shoppableImage`, `collectionHero`, `imageText`, `hotspotPopup/Marker`, `definitions.ts`). Barrel: `overrides/app/components/contentful/index.ts`. - **Types:** `overrides/app/types/contentful.ts`. **Product-adjacent Contentful content today:** the closest is `overrides/app/components/contentful/productHero.tsx`. Notably, it does **not** pull product copy from Contentful — it takes a Contentful-authored SFCC product **id** (`productHero` field) and resolves the actual data (`name`, `shortDescription`/`longDescription`, images) from **SFCC** via `useProduct` from `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react`. It supports Contentful Live Preview via `ContentfulLivePreview.getProps`. This is the canonical example of the ownership rule: **Contentful references the product; SFCC owns the attributes.** **Doc:** `.docs/integration/02-contentful.md` is the relevant doc. Key points for a PDP accordion: - Ownership table (§1): for **PDP**, SFCC owns product attributes/price/inventory/variations/gallery; Contentful owns marketing copy, editorial blocks, size-guide fallback. Crucially the PDP row and Open Item #2 (§10) both say **which blocks are Contentful vs SFCC Page Designer is still *pending***. - So **care instructions / sustainability (Environmental Qualities) are NOT confirmed as Contentful** — the PRD says Environmental Qualities comes from **AP21**, and product-copy ownership is explicitly TBD. Do not assume Contentful sourcing for accordion body content without confirmation. - SSR-first for PDP editorial; graceful degradation (empty editorial slots never block commerce data). --- ### 5. Component / override conventions A new component belongs under `overrides/app/components//`. Representative existing custom component — `overrides/app/components/button/`: - `index.tsx` — named export `export const Button` (+ props type `ButtonProps` declared at top), TypeScript, wraps Chakra primitives, styling delegated to the theme (`overrides/app/theme/components/button.ts`). - `index.stories.tsx` — Storybook 8.6 CSF3, `title: 'Elements/Button'`, `Default` + state exports. Folder-naming rule (from `.claude/skills/new-component/SKILL.md`): **`componentName/` (camelCase) for Zimmermann-authored** components, **`component-name/` (kebab-case) when overriding a base SF component**. Since the base is `product-detail/partials/information-accordion.jsx`, an override-style component would be kebab-case; a fresh Zimmermann component would be camelCase. Other conventions from the skill and rules it references (`.claude/rules/conventions.md`, `components.md`, `css.md`): - Import base package via the `@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` alias — **never** from `node_modules/...` source directly. - Presentational components take data as **props**; parents/pages own data fetching (no commerce/React-Query hooks inside a leaf component). `productHero.tsx` is a mild exception because it's a container. - Chakra tokens only — no hardcoded hex/px/font sizes. - Story categories: `Foundation/ Elements/ Layout/ Commerce/ Forms/ Pages/ Contentful/`. A product-info accordion would likely be `Commerce/`. - Story mandatory; Vitest only for non-trivial logic; run `npx tsc --noEmit` after. Existing folder layouts range from a single `index.tsx` (`header/`, `pageContainer/`) to `index.tsx` + `index.stories.tsx` (`button/`) to multi-file (`icons/`: `index.tsx`, `icons.stories.tsx`, `zimm.tsx`; `contentful/` with a barrel `index.ts` + `experiences/` subfolder). --- ### Key file paths (repo-relative) - `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/product-detail/index.jsx` — base PDP (renders `InformationAccordion` at lines 776 & 808) - `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/product-detail/partials/information-accordion.jsx` — the base accordion to refactor - `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/theme/components/base/accordion.js` — accordion base theme - `overrides/app/routes.tsx` — confirms PDP route inherited (no override) - `overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts` — Contentful fetch hooks - `overrides/app/config/contentful.ts`, `overrides/app/config/contentfulMapping.ts` — Contentful config/mapping - `overrides/app/components/contentful/productHero.tsx` — product-ref-from-Contentful, data-from-SFCC pattern - `overrides/app/components/button/` — representative custom component (folder convention) - `.claude/skills/new-component/SKILL.md` — scaffolding conventions - `.docs/prd/pdp.md` — target accordion spec (§lines 11, 130-146: Details/Size&Fit/Care/Shipping; Size Guide; EU Environmental Qualities) - `.docs/integration/02-contentful.md` — Contentful ownership/architecture (PDP block ownership still *pending*, §1 + §10) One caveat worth flagging for the story split: the base accordion's items (Reviews, Questions) do **not** match the PRD's items (Care, Shipping & Free Returns), and the data sources for the PRD accordions are mixed/unconfirmed (SFCC `longDescription` today, AP21 for Environmental Qualities, Contentful for size-guide fallback, product-copy ownership TBD). That mismatch and the source ambiguity are the main seams to slice the story along.

I have everything needed. Here is my research report. ## Summary This is retail-react-app **v10.0.0**. The PDP is **not overridden** in this repo — it runs entirely from the base template. The product-information accordion is a small, self-contained partial in the base package, and the repo already has a working Contentful integration pattern (hooks + typed components + config) that a new PDP accordion could plug into. --- ### 1. PDP page structure **No PDP override exists.** `overrides/app/pages/` contains only: `contentfulPreview/`, `experience/`, `home/`, `my-new-route/`. There is no `product-detail/`. The PDP is served entirely from the base template: - `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/product-detail/index.jsx` (~39 KB, the main page) - `.../product-detail/partials/information-accordion.jsx` (the only partial) - `.../product-detail/index.mock.js`, `index.test.js` Routing confirms this: `overrides/app/routes.tsx` spreads the base routes via `..._routes` and adds no `product-detail` entry, so the PDP route is inherited unchanged. **Composition** (from `index.jsx`): the page fetches product/category data, sets SEO via `Helmet`, then renders (all repo-relative to the base package): - `app/components/product-view` — `ProductView` (gallery, name, price, variation attributes, add-to-cart/wishlist). Wrapped in an `Island` with `hydrateOn="visible"`. - `app/pages/product-detail/partials/information-accordion` — `InformationAccordion`, rendered **right after** `ProductView` (line 808 for a normal product; line 776 for each child of a set/bundle). - `app/components/recommended-products` — `RecommendedProducts` (Einstein "Complete the Set" / "You might also like"), each in its own `Island`. So the accordion is a peer of `ProductView`, taking `product` as its only prop. --- ### 2. Accordion usage **Base product-information accordion:** `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/product-detail/partials/information-accordion.jsx` (121 lines). It imports Chakra `Accordion, AccordionItem, AccordionButton, AccordionPanel, AccordionIcon` from `app/components/shared/ui` and renders a hardcoded `` with **four fixed items**: 1. **"Product Detail"** — renders `product?.longDescription` via `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` 2. **"Size & Fit"** — hardcoded "Coming Soon" 3. **"Reviews"** — "Coming Soon" 4. **"Questions"** — "Coming Soon" Each item is a `

...

` + ``. Items are not data-driven or conditionally rendered — they always render, even when empty. Message IDs follow `product_detail.accordion.button.*` / `product_detail.accordion.message.coming_soon`. **Accordion theming:** `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/theme/components/base/accordion.js` (base styles: `button.paddingLeft: 0`, no hover bg). The overrides theme (`overrides/app/theme/components/`) does **not** currently customize the accordion. **Other accordion in base (not PDP):** `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/nested-accordion/` + `app/theme/components/project/nested-accordion.js` — used for nested category/refinement menus, not product information. **Accordion usage in `overrides/`: none.** A grep for `Accordion` across `overrides/` returned zero matches. --- ### 3. Existing product information / tabs components The only such component is the base `information-accordion.jsx` above. There is **no** Tabs-based product-info component, no `product-information` component, and no "Details & Care" / "Shipping & Returns" / "Materials" component anywhere in `overrides/` or the base PDP. The strings "Details & Care", "Shipping & Returns", "Materials", "Care" do not exist in the base PDP — only "Product Detail", "Size & Fit", "Reviews", "Questions". **The PRD is where the target design lives** — `.docs/prd/pdp.md`: - Line 11 (PRD-008, confirmed): "Key supporting information in expandable accordions: **Details, Size & Fit, Care, Shipping & Free Returns** (region-specific content)". This is the real accordion the story targets — it differs from the base's Reviews/Questions items. - §12 (PRD-009, confirmed), lines 142-146: a separate **"Environmental Qualities / AGEC" accordion**, EU storefronts only (`/en-eu/`, `/fr-eu/`), **data sourced from AP21**, and **only renders when data exists** (no empty accordion). - §11 (lines 130-138): Size guide is a **Measmerize slide-out overlay**, with a **Contentful-managed content type as fallback** per product type — separate from the accordion. - Line 20 / 216: **product copy ownership (description/editorial) is still TBD** — Contentful vs SFCC vs AP21. These are natural seams for splitting the story: (a) refactor base accordion into a data-driven Zimmermann component with the correct item set, (b) Care/region-specific content wiring, (c) EU-only Environmental Qualities accordion (AP21 data, conditional render), (d) Size & Fit / size-guide overlay hookup. --- ### 4. Contentful integration for PDP The repo has a complete, custom Contentful pattern under `overrides/app/`: - **Config:** `overrides/app/config/contentful.ts` — `getContentfulConfig()` pulls `app.contentful` from `getConfig()` (space/env/delivery+preview tokens, sourced from `config/default.js`). Plus `overrides/app/config/contentfulMapping.ts` (+ `.generated.ts`) mapping SFCC site IDs → locales and MRT tiers → Contentful environments. Registered content types are minimal so far: `CONTENT_TYPE_IDS = { shoppableImage }`. - **Hooks:** `overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts` — `useContentfulEntry(entryId, preview)` and `useContentfulEntries(contentType, preview)`. Client-side `fetch` against CDA/CPA with `include=2`, resolves linked assets, `AbortController` cleanup. - **Components:** `overrides/app/components/contentful/` — `heroBanner`, `duplexSection`, `videoEmbed`, `productHero`, plus `experiences/` (Studio Experiences: `shoppableImage`, `collectionHero`, `imageText`, `hotspotPopup/Marker`, `definitions.ts`). Barrel: `overrides/app/components/contentful/index.ts`. - **Types:** `overrides/app/types/contentful.ts`. **Product-adjacent Contentful content today:** the closest is `overrides/app/components/contentful/productHero.tsx`. Notably, it does **not** pull product copy from Contentful — it takes a Contentful-authored SFCC product **id** (`productHero` field) and resolves the actual data (`name`, `shortDescription`/`longDescription`, images) from **SFCC** via `useProduct` from `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react`. It supports Contentful Live Preview via `ContentfulLivePreview.getProps`. This is the canonical example of the ownership rule: **Contentful references the product; SFCC owns the attributes.** **Doc:** `.docs/integration/02-contentful.md` is the relevant doc. Key points for a PDP accordion: - Ownership table (§1): for **PDP**, SFCC owns product attributes/price/inventory/variations/gallery; Contentful owns marketing copy, editorial blocks, size-guide fallback. Crucially the PDP row and Open Item #2 (§10) both say **which blocks are Contentful vs SFCC Page Designer is still *pending***. - So **care instructions / sustainability (Environmental Qualities) are NOT confirmed as Contentful** — the PRD says Environmental Qualities comes from **AP21**, and product-copy ownership is explicitly TBD. Do not assume Contentful sourcing for accordion body content without confirmation. - SSR-first for PDP editorial; graceful degradation (empty editorial slots never block commerce data). --- ### 5. Component / override conventions A new component belongs under `overrides/app/components//`. Representative existing custom component — `overrides/app/components/button/`: - `index.tsx` — named export `export const Button` (+ props type `ButtonProps` declared at top), TypeScript, wraps Chakra primitives, styling delegated to the theme (`overrides/app/theme/components/button.ts`). - `index.stories.tsx` — Storybook 8.6 CSF3, `title: 'Elements/Button'`, `Default` + state exports. Folder-naming rule (from `.claude/skills/new-component/SKILL.md`): **`componentName/` (camelCase) for Zimmermann-authored** components, **`component-name/` (kebab-case) when overriding a base SF component**. Since the base is `product-detail/partials/information-accordion.jsx`, an override-style component would be kebab-case; a fresh Zimmermann component would be camelCase. Other conventions from the skill and rules it references (`.claude/rules/conventions.md`, `components.md`, `css.md`): - Import base package via the `@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` alias — **never** from `node_modules/...` source directly. - Presentational components take data as **props**; parents/pages own data fetching (no commerce/React-Query hooks inside a leaf component). `productHero.tsx` is a mild exception because it's a container. - Chakra tokens only — no hardcoded hex/px/font sizes. - Story categories: `Foundation/ Elements/ Layout/ Commerce/ Forms/ Pages/ Contentful/`. A product-info accordion would likely be `Commerce/`. - Story mandatory; Vitest only for non-trivial logic; run `npx tsc --noEmit` after. Existing folder layouts range from a single `index.tsx` (`header/`, `pageContainer/`) to `index.tsx` + `index.stories.tsx` (`button/`) to multi-file (`icons/`: `index.tsx`, `icons.stories.tsx`, `zimm.tsx`; `contentful/` with a barrel `index.ts` + `experiences/` subfolder). --- ### Key file paths (repo-relative) - `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/product-detail/index.jsx` — base PDP (renders `InformationAccordion` at lines 776 & 808) - `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/product-detail/partials/information-accordion.jsx` — the base accordion to refactor - `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/theme/components/base/accordion.js` — accordion base theme - `overrides/app/routes.tsx` — confirms PDP route inherited (no override) - `overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts` — Contentful fetch hooks - `overrides/app/config/contentful.ts`, `overrides/app/config/contentfulMapping.ts` — Contentful config/mapping - `overrides/app/components/contentful/productHero.tsx` — product-ref-from-Contentful, data-from-SFCC pattern - `overrides/app/components/button/` — representative custom component (folder convention) - `.claude/skills/new-component/SKILL.md` — scaffolding conventions - `.docs/prd/pdp.md` — target accordion spec (§lines 11, 130-146: Details/Size&Fit/Care/Shipping; Size Guide; EU Environmental Qualities) - `.docs/integration/02-contentful.md` — Contentful ownership/architecture (PDP block ownership still *pending*, §1 + §10) One caveat worth flagging for the story split: the base accordion's items (Reviews, Questions) do **not** match the PRD's items (Care, Shipping & Free Returns), and the data sources for the PRD accordions are mixed/unconfirmed (SFCC `longDescription` today, AP21 for Environmental Qualities, Contentful for size-guide fallback, product-copy ownership TBD). That mismatch and the source ambiguity are the main seams to slice the story along.

# PRD – Product Detail Page (PDP)

*Source of truth: Zimmermann Functional Requirements.xlsx, sheets "Product, Catalogue and PDP" (PRD), "Cart & Inventory" (CAI), "Payments" (PAY), "Returns and Refunds" (RRC), "Customers, Account, CRM Sync" (CRM), "Order Management" (OM). Last updated: 2026-06-19.*

---

## 1. Page Structure

- Breadcrumb navigation displayed on all PDP pages (PRD-001, confirmed)
- Style code (SKU) displayed on PDP (PRD-007, confirmed)
- Key supporting information in expandable accordions: **Details, Size & Fit, Care, Shipping & Free Returns** (region-specific content) (PRD-008, confirmed)

---

## 2. Product Data

- Product name, price, sizes, and colour swatches sourced from the **Product API** (fed from AP21, but AP21 may not be the sole source in future — do not hard-code AP21 as the only data provider). Colour swatch assets do not live in AP21 — only colour names (PRD-002, confirmed — requirement updated for clarity 05.05)
- Style code (SKU) from product data (PRD-007, confirmed)
- "Also available in" / "Only available in" colour swatches; selecting a colour updates the page content and URL (PRD-004, confirmed). Hover-to-preview swatch behaviour (colour updates on rollover without click) is a **custom build, not OOTB, and not scoped for go-live** — see Open Items (PRD-004)
- *Open: product copy ownership (description, editorial text) — Contentful vs SFCC vs AP21 is TBD (see AGENTS.md "Unresolved Dependencies")*

---

## 3. Product Badges & Tags (PRD-005 – PRD-006, confirmed)

- Products can carry one or more badges: **Campaign, Runway, Exclusive, Online Exclusive, VIC Exclusive** — badge *assignment* on applicable products is confirmed (PRD-005)
- Multiple badges per product are supported; a defined display priority/hierarchy applies when more than one badge is present
- Badge creation must not require a code deployment (PRD-005, comment: "ideally the creation of these badges would not require a code change")
- **Badges are clickable** and navigate the customer to a PLP view filtered to products in that badge category (PRD-005, confirmed — workbook updated 2026-06-19: "captured in requirement"). See also plp.md §2.6.
- *Design caveat: badges not yet present in PLP designs ("Missing badges in PLP") (PRD-005)*

---

## 4. Product States (PRD-010 – PRD-017, confirmed)

- **Coming Soon** — product is displayed on PDP before stock is added or purchase is enabled
- **Back in Soon** — product has sold out but will restock imminently (re-cut)
- **Unavailable (size-level)** — triggers the Notify Me flow for the affected size variant
- OOS sizes visually greyed out/disabled; Add to Bag is suppressed for that size variant (PRD-014)
- All product states (Coming Soon, Back in Soon, Unavailable) must comply with **Google Merchant Centre** feed rules — ineligible-state products must not surface in product feeds (PRD-017)
- Low-stock indicator at size level: displays **"LOW"** label — purely visual, does not alter CTA behaviour or block add-to-bag (PRD-012; also PRD-030 from CAI)

---

## 5. Pricing Display

- Display price in storefront currency (AUD, USD, GBP, EUR)
- Sale pricing: was/now format (PRD-003, confirmed — subject to designs). If price changes again after being put on sale, only "now" updates; "was" is retained (REG-042, confirmed)
- Tax label per storefront: GST (AU), VAT (UK/EU), Tax (US) (PAY, confirmed)
- **Duties and taxes information** displayed country-specifically on PDP (PRD-013, confirmed)
- **DDP/DDU messaging** displayed on PDP per applicable countries (PAY-059, confirmed)
- Max configurable purchase quantity enforced per customer group (PRD-011, confirmed)
- *Open: HK/ME/US Intl/EU Intl pricing display — Global-e pricing via SFCC price books is defined and REG-041 is confirmed (REG-040 retired). Sign-off of the full mechanism (PRC-34..PRC-43) is still pending; do not implement until confirmed.*

---

## 6. Availability & Add to Bag

*Buffer stock rules apply on PDP. See [cart.md](cart.md) section 5 for the full buffer stock system.*

- Per-size availability shown (ADD TO BAG / OUT OF STOCK / low-stock "LOW" indicator)
- **ADD TO BAG** shown when quantity is above buffer threshold
- **OUT OF STOCK** shown when quantity is at or below buffer threshold (back-in-stock capture presented)
- Low-stock indicator at size level — no quantity number shown — displays "LOW" label
- **Max 3 units per SKU** (same size + colour) enforced at add-to-cart (CAI-017, confirmed)
- **No soft reservation** at add-to-cart (CAI-032, confirmed)

---

## 7. Primary CTAs & Supporting Links (PRD-018 – PRD-022, confirmed)

- **Add to Bag** — primary CTA when in stock
- **Find in Boutique** — opens as a **slide-out** (not a modal) alongside Add to Bag (PRD-018)
- **Wishlist icon** — displayed alongside the primary CTA; size must be selected before wishlist save (PRD-019, PRD-020)
- Supporting links: **Unavailable** (opens slide-out notify me form), **Find My Size**, **Size Guide** (PRD-021)
- **Need Assistance** section: links to email, live chat (with availability hours caveat), and Contact Us (PRD-022). The "Contact Us" link is an external redirect to the Zendesk-hosted contact form — there is no embedded Zendesk integration in the storefront.

---

## 8. Find in Boutique (CAI-037 – CAI-042, PRD-028 – PRD-039)

The "Find in Boutique" CTA is shown on all eligible products. The feature opens as a **flyout/slide-out panel** (not a modal). All Find in Boutique requirements are now **confirmed** but carry a **Phase 2** design caveat (design not yet available — "Phase 2").

### Panel contents
- "Find in Boutique" CTA only displays for products where in-store stock checking is supported (PRD-028, confirmed — Phase 2 design)
- At top of panel: product thumbnail, product name, selected colour, and price (PRD-029, confirmed — Phase 2 design)
- **Size selector** pre-populated from the PDP selection; customer can change size within the panel (PRD-030, confirmed — Phase 2 design)
- A **real-time inventory call** to NewStore via MuleSoft is made once a size is selected; the call refreshes when the customer selects a different size (CAI-038)
- **No auto-refresh** while the panel is open; boutique stock cached with configurable TTL (CAI-042)
- **Location search field** to filter boutique results (PRD-031, confirmed — Phase 2 design)
- **"Use My Location"** option triggers browser geolocation with explicit permission; handles failure case gracefully with inline message (PRD-032, PRD-033, confirmed — Phase 2 design)
- **Maps integration** via Google Maps (via MRT API connection) for boutique directions (PRD-034, confirmed — Phase 2 design)
- Per-boutique results show: name, address, distance (if geolocation permitted), stock status (**In Stock / Low Stock – Contact Boutique to Confirm Availability / Out of Stock**), opening hours, contact details, current live open status (e.g. "OPEN – CLOSES AT 6:00PM"), map pin, and a view more button (PRD-035, confirmed). Opening hours and live open status are sourced from the **Google Business API** (with a manual override available in Business Manager) — distinct from the Google Maps integration used for the map pin and directions (TPI: Google Business API; Google Maps).
- **Get Directions** link per boutique result, opening the location in a maps application (PRD-036, confirmed)
- Configurable limit on number of boutique results displayed (PRD-039, confirmed)
- Display a clear message when no boutiques carry the selected size (CAI-041)
- **No buffer stock** applied to boutique inventory (CAI-040)
- Fully responsive across desktop, tablet, and mobile (PRD-037, confirmed)
- Enter key triggers search in the location field (PRD-038, confirmed)

---

## 9. Back-in-Stock Notifications / Stock Alert (OM-033 – OM-034, PRD-040 – PRD-049, confirmed)

Shown when product/size is OOS (Unavailable state):

- Stock alert CTA/link displayed on PDP when selected size is OOS (PRD-040)
- Opens as a slide-out with the stock alert sign-up form: product name, price, and product image thumbnail at top (PRD-041, PRD-042)
- **Multiple size selection supported** — customer selects which unavailable sizes to register for (PRD-043)
- Customer name and email captured as required fields; **pre-populated and editable for authenticated customers** (PRD-044)
- **Marketing opt-in/out checkbox** compliant with regional consent requirements, gated by Omneo consent management (PRD-045)
- Clear submission CTA to register the stock alert (PRD-046)
- Confirmation message shown within the slide-out on successful submission (PRD-047)
- Notifications sent **FIFO** to first configurable-N (default 30) customers when stock returns above buffer; if stock is still available after a configurable time window (default 30 minutes), the next batch of 30 receives the email (PRD-048)
- Stock replenishment signal flows from NewStore → MuleSoft → SFCC → email trigger (PRD-049)
- No loyalty tier prioritisation

---

## 10. Find My Size / Measmerize (PRD-050 – PRD-053)

The Measmerize widget is embedded on PDP and manages the Find My Size experience:

- Once Measmerize generates a recommendation, the system updates the CTA to display **"Recommended: Size X"** (PRD-050 — Measmerize widget manages behaviour)
- When the customer clicks "Recommended", the Measmerize widget handles navigation to the recommendation view — SFCC does not control this flow (PRD-051 removed as not applicable for SFCC)
- Whether the "Find My Size" link is shown/suppressed based on Measmerize data availability is managed by the Measmerize widget, not SFCC (PRD-052 removed as not applicable for SFCC)

---

## 11. Size Guide (PRD-053 – PRD-057, confirmed)

- Size guide opens as a **slide-out overlay** (not a modal) without navigating away from the PDP (PRD-053, confirmed)
- Size guide content is delivered via the **Measmerize overlay** (confirmed — VR/RT comment resolved 2026-06-19: "Yes is going to be a measmerize overlay"). The Contentful-managed size guide is shown as a fallback only where no Measmerize data exists for a given product.
- *SEO/LLM risk (acknowledged, not blocking): Measmerize is a third-party overlay; content rendered within it may not be indexable by search engines or LLMs. The decision to use Measmerize is made; this risk is noted for the team to monitor.*
- Size conversion tables appropriate to the selected product type (PRD-054)
- Size guide content managed as a **structured Contentful content type** per product type (Ready to Wear, Swim, Accessories, Belts, Jewellery, Men's, Denim, Hats, etc.) (PRD-055)
- **Measurement toggle: cm / inches** (PRD-056)
- Size guide content manageable without a code deployment — content managed via CMS (PRD-057, confirmed 2026-05-25)

---

## 12. EU Environmental Qualities / AGEC (PRD-009, confirmed)

- Environmental Qualities accordion rendered on EU storefronts (`/en-eu/`, `/fr-eu/`) only
- Data sourced from AP21
- **Only renders when data exists** — no placeholder or empty accordion shown

---

## 13. Content Modules

### As Seen / Seen on the Runway editorial module (PRD-023, confirmed)
- CMS-managed editorial imagery module per product or collection (per new designs, surfaced as "Seen on the Runway"). Confirmed subject to designs.

### Shop the Look (PRD-024, confirmed)
- "Shop the Look" module displayed on PDP; clicking a product navigates to its PDP
- Auto-hides if no related products are populated; excludes out-of-stock products

### Styling module (PRD-025, confirmed — requirement updated 06.05)
- Styling is part of the Shop the Look module (same thing) — treat as a Shop the Look variant, not a separate module.
- Applies to **dresses and jewellery**; must auto-hide if related content/products are not populated; must **not** display for kids, men's, or other accessories.

### You May Also Like (PRD-026, SPR-58, confirmed)
- "You May Also Like" carousel powered by SFCC Einstein; rules-based fallback at launch
- Note: design refers to this as "More Colourful x" — implement per final designs

### Recently Viewed (PRD-027, SPR-61, confirmed)
- "Recently Viewed" carousel / "See Full History"/"See All" button (design TBC) based on browsing session
- Session-based for guests; persists cross-session for logged-in customers

---

## 14. Product Imagery & Media (PRD-058 – PRD-070)

- Multiple images per product: front, back, detail, and model shots (PRD-058, confirmed)
- Thumbnail gallery navigation (PRD-059, confirmed)
- **Hover-to-zoom or click-to-expand lightbox** on primary image — desktop (PRD-060, confirmed)

- Primary hero image **priority-loaded** (may vary per product — flatlay, model, or video) (PRD-064, confirmed)

- Video autoplay configurable per video instance without a code deployment (PRD-068, ready for sign off)
- Flexible image presentation per page type (configurable background colour/treatment) without asset duplication (PRD-069, ready for sign off)
- Alt text required on all product images before a product can be published (PRD-070, ready for sign off)
- *Open: Video hosting platform — Vimeo is under consideration but not confirmed. Action open to confirm the best solution for smoothest FE experience (PRD-067). Note: the Third Party Integrations sheet lists Vimeo as the media platform (embed URL stored in product data or CMS); this conflicts with PRD-067's challenging comment ("Vimeo has not been 100% confirmed") — treat as Open until the open action resolves.*

I've got what I need. Before writing, one honesty note: I searched the tickets for Tim's verbatim "component-based" comment and couldn't isolate his exact words (comment-author filtering isn't well supported, and the phrase search came back empty). But his direction is already concretely embodied in how the team has been structuring recent tickets, so I can point you at the working pattern rather than a quote.

Here's my read.

## Short version

Jasmin's instinct is right — split it, and split the reusable shell out from the content. That's exactly Tim's component-based direction and it matches what the team is already doing elsewhere. But **"shell + one story per tab" splits along the wrong seam.** Four of the five tabs are structurally identical; the thing that actually differs (and carries the build effort, risk, and acceptance criteria) is the **data source and gating logic**, not the tab label. I'd do **4 stories split by data source**, not 6.

## What Tim's "component-based" direction actually looks like here

The team already has a live template for this. On the filters work it's a three-part decomposition:

- [SFCC-104](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-104) — *Filters & Facets — BM Configuration (Shared)* → the backend/config enabler
- [SFCC-108](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-108) — *Search Results – Filters & Facets UI **Component*** → the shared component, built once
- [SFCC-199](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-199) — *PLP UI – Filters & Facets **Component*** → whose description literally reads *"it is a shared filter panel component like in SFCC-108… It scopes the integration of that component into the PLP page template"*

[SFCC-83](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-83) (*Recently Viewed UI Component (Shared)*) is the same idea: *"built once and reused across multiple page contexts."* And note [SFCC-83](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-83) split the **consent** concern out into its own story ([SFCC-106](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-106)) — cross-cutting behaviour became its own slice.

So the pattern Tim's pushing is: **(shared enabler) → (reusable component) → (per-context integration), and peel cross-cutting behaviour into its own story.** The unit of a story is a *seam*, not a *tab*.

Also worth knowing: your own [SFCC-89](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-89) (*PDP UI — Static Product Information*, assigned to you, Blocked) already **explicitly carved the accordion out** — its "Out of scope" list names *"Accordion content (Details & Care, Size & Fit, Shipping & Returns)"* and *"Contentful-sourced content."* SFCC-195 is that carve-out. So the top-level split already exists; this is about how finely to slice 195 itself.

## Why "one story per tab" is the wrong seam

Map the five tabs to their data path (from the [SFCC-195](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-195) description + [.docs/prd/pdp.md](.docs/prd/pdp.md) §1, §12):

| Tab | Data source | Notable behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| Details & Care | **SFCC** product attribute | HTML → sanitize → render |
| Size & Fit | **SFCC** product attribute | same path (+ unconfirmed new attribute, see below) |
| Shipping & Returns | **Contentful** | region-specific rich text |
| Assistance | **Contentful** (or region config?) | links: email / chat / Contact Us (Zendesk external, PRD-022) |
| Environmental Qualities | **AP21** | EU-only, renders *only if data exists* (PRD-009) |

Four of these are "title + expandable panel of rendered rich text." Splitting them per-tab gives you 4 near-clone stories that differ only by which content key they read — that's config, not a story's worth of independent build and QA. It also produces stories that **aren't independently demoable** (a lone "Assistance tab" can't ship without the shell), which breaks INVEST, and it multiplies the ceremony (refinement, PR, review, BrowserStack/Zephyr per-story runs) ~6× for what is really one component + three data adapters.

## What I'd propose instead — 4 stories, split by data source

| # | Story | Covers | Source | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A** | PDP – Product Information Accordion (shell + Details & Care) | Reusable accordion container **plus the first real tab as a walking skeleton**: Chakra `Accordion` override of the base partial, WCAG 2.2 AA, theme registration, ordering, empty-tab suppression, SSR-rendered for SEO, EU-conditional slot | SFCC | Copy-first PDP override; [SFCC-26](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-26) |
| **B** | PDP – Size & Fit accordion content | Size & Fit panel (same SFCC path as A) | SFCC | A; [SFCC-26](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-26); new "model size / size & fit" attribute confirmation |
| **C** | PDP – Contentful accordion content | Shipping & Returns + Assistance (region-keyed rich text — one data path) | Contentful | A; [SFCC-249](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-249) content model; ownership sign-off |
| **D** | PDP – EU Environmental Qualities accordion | EU-only, conditional render, distinct source | AP21 | A; AP21 attribute; EU storefront config ([SFCC-151](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-151)) |

Key move: **give the shell a real tab (Details & Care) so story A is a vertical slice** — demoable and independently valuable — instead of a "shell with nothing in it" horizontal slice. D stays separate because it genuinely differs (regional gating + AP21 + render-only-if-present; it even has its own requirement, PRD-009). This collapses to **3 stories** if you'd rather fold Size & Fit into A (same data path). I'd only go to Jasmin's full 6-way split if the accordion or individual tabs were going to be **reused on other page types** — they're not; Chakra already gives us the accordion primitive, so a standalone shell story buys little.

## Three things to resolve before finalising the split (these decide the slicing)

1. **Content ownership is still officially open.** The [SFCC-195](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-195) description asserts a mapping (Details & Care + Size & Fit = SFCC; the rest = Contentful), but [.docs/prd/pdp.md](.docs/prd/pdp.md) §18 lists *"Product copy ownership (Contentful vs SFCC vs AP21) — TBD"* as an open item, and [.docs/integration/02-contentful.md](.docs/integration/02-contentful.md) says the PDP block ownership is still pending. Per our doc-integrity rule the ticket shouldn't pre-empt an open PRD item — worth confirming the source-of-truth mapping first, because stories C and D are *defined by* it. In particular: is **Assistance** really Contentful editorial, or is it static links / region config (PRD-022)?
2. **Contentful content model isn't landed yet.** [SFCC-249](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-249) (*Contentful Integration Technical Design & Content Model*) is only in Code Review. Story C is blocked until the accordion content types exist — sequence it after that.
3. **The SFCC "Size & Fit" attribute is unconfirmed.** [SFCC-89](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-89)'s comment flags that model size/fit needs a *new* product attribute ("to discuss with Dani"), and SFCC-89 is Blocked partly by [SFCC-26](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-26). Story B inherits that.

## One codebase reality to factor in

There is **no PDP override in the repo yet** — the PDP runs entirely from the base template, and the accordion is a hardcoded 4-item partial (`product-detail/partials/information-accordion.jsx` — Product Detail / Size & Fit / Reviews / Questions) that doesn't match our tab set. Story A is therefore a **copy-first override** of the PDP partial into `overrides/`, replacing it with a data-driven Zimmermann component (`Commerce/` in Storybook). The Contentful plumbing already exists (`overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts`, and the *"Contentful references the product, SFCC owns the attributes"* pattern in `overrides/app/components/contentful/productHero.tsx`), so C plugs into an established path.

# 14 — Inside Chat (Customer Service Chat)

## 1. Purpose and scope

Inside Chat (by Powerfront) is the customer-service live chat widget on Zimmermann storefronts.

Per HPC-039/040, the widget is a **direct PWA head tag** — not loaded via GTM. In the previous Magento implementation Tryzens hardcoded the script in the page head. The PWA is to follow the same pattern. Vicky@Zimmermann confirmed this approach as best practice (2026-07-02).

The PWA loads the Inside Chat script asynchronously, post-Didomi-consent, so it never blocks first paint. The site token (`INSIDE_CHAT_SITE_TOKEN`) is a public identifier held as an MRT environment variable and embedded in the script tag at load time.

Page visibility rules and widget configuration are owned by Zimmermann / Inside Chat / Tryzens — outside PWA scope.

## 2. PWA implementation summary

| Concern        | Detail                                                        |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Load mechanism | Direct PWA head tag — async script inject post-Didomi-consent |
| Env var        | `INSIDE_CHAT_SITE_TOKEN` (public; safe in bundle)             |
| Consent gate   | Didomi — consent category TBC (Zimmermann Privacy to confirm) |
| Scope          | All storefronts                                               |
| LCP impact     | None — async, post-consent, never on critical path            |

## 3. Open items

1. **The script tag / site token.** From Zimmermann / Inside Chat / Tryzens (the equivalent of what Tryzens hardcoded in Magento)
2. **Didomi consent category and vendor / feature ID.** Zimmermann to confirm the Didomi vendor or feature ID so the consent-gated loader can be wired. **Owner:** Zimmermann Privacy / Tell No Lies.

1	# Learning Log — Reviewing a Motion Design Prototype as FED Lead
2	
3	**Date:** 2026-08-07
4	**Context:** Jon (motion designer) sent through a homepage masthead motion prototype (`HomeMasthead.mov`). My manager asked me + Bianca to review it, compile questions, and confirm the "absolute must-haves" before we capture motion-design user stories. Tim also chimed in with a one-line concern.
5	**Role lens:** Front-End Development Lead (spans both squads). I'm Claude-assisted, so this log is where I make the reasoning *mine* rather than just shipping the output.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## 0. Why this log exists
10	
11	The deliverable (a clean question list for Jon) is the easy part to copy. The *reusable* part is:
12	1. **How** I turned a 50-second video into verifiable facts.
13	2. **The lens** I applied — how a FED Lead pressure-tests a design against *this* project's hard constraints.
14	3. **How** I compressed a thorough technical review into a message a stakeholder actually reads.
15	
16	Those three things transfer to every future design/motion review. The specific questions about this one masthead don't.
17	
18	---
19	
20	## 1. Lesson: verify the artefact, don't narrate it
21	
22	My first instinct (and the team's) was to *describe* the video from memory. That produced three wrong or incomplete "facts" that would have gone to Jon:
23	
24	| What we said | What the pixels actually showed |
25	| --- | --- |
26	| Video controls are "audio + fullscreen" | Controls are **mute/unmute + play/pause**. No fullscreen exists. |
27	| Tile hover "instantly switches" image | It's a **cross-dissolve/slide**, not an instant switch. |
28	| (not noticed) | Hover also **reveals the price** and **prev/next arrows**. |
29	| (not noticed) | Body copy is **placeholder** (same paragraph repeated twice). |
30	
31	**Takeaway:** a reviewer's credibility dies the moment a stakeholder spots something they claimed that isn't true. Before sending observations upstream, confirm them against the source frame-by-frame. "I watched it once" is not verification.
32	
33	### Technique — watching a video when you have no ffmpeg
34	
35	This machine had no `ffmpeg`/`ffprobe`, but macOS ships Swift + AVFoundation. This extracts frames at an interval and can crop/upscale a region for detail (e.g. reading tiny UI controls). Keep this snippet — it's the fastest way to inspect any `.mov`/`.mp4` on a Mac with zero installs.
36	
37	```swift
38	// swift extract.swift  — dumps JPEG frames every `interval` seconds
39	import AVFoundation; import AppKit; import Foundation
40	let asset = AVURLAsset(url: URL(fileURLWithPath: "/path/to/video.mov"))
41	let gen = AVAssetImageGenerator(asset: asset)
42	gen.appliesPreferredTrackTransform = true
43	gen.requestedTimeToleranceBefore = .zero   // exact frame, not nearest keyframe
44	gen.requestedTimeToleranceAfter  = .zero
45	let dur = CMTimeGetSeconds(asset.duration), interval = 1.7
46	var t = 0.0, i = 0
47	while t < dur {
48	    if let cg = try? gen.copyCGImage(at: CMTime(seconds: t, preferredTimescale: 600), actualTime: nil) {
49	        let rep = NSBitmapImageRep(cgImage: cg)
50	        let data = rep.representation(using: .jpeg, properties: [.compressionFactor: 0.7])!
51	        try? data.write(to: URL(fileURLWithPath: String(format: "frames/f%02d.jpg", i)))
52	    }
53	    i += 1; t += interval
54	}
55	```
56	
57	- To read tiny UI (video controls, icons): re-run **without** `maximumSize`, then `cg.cropping(to: rect)` a small region and redraw it into a larger `CGContext` with `.high` interpolation. Reading the `‖` pause glyph vs a fullscreen icon is only possible at full res.
58	- `mdls -name kMDItemDurationSeconds -name kMDItemPixelWidth -name kMDItemPixelHeight file.mov` gives you duration/resolution instantly with no tooling.
59	- **Read the metadata, not just the picture:** the file was 1438px wide and named `HomeMasthead` — that alone told me this is a **desktop, masthead-only** proto, which reframed half the review (mobile + full page are simply out of scope of what was delivered).
60	
61	---
62	
63	## 2. Lesson: the FED Lead lens = pressure-test the design against the project's *hard* constraints
64	
65	Anyone can list what a prototype does. The value I add is mapping it against the non-negotiables in `AGENTS.md` and `.claude/rules/`. This is the reusable framework — run any new UI/motion design through these gates:
66	
67	### a) Performance budget (the one that kills homepages)
68	- **Budget:** LCP ≤ 2s at p75 mobile (`AGENTS.md > Performance`). A full-bleed **autoplay hero video** is the textbook way to blow this.
69	- Reflexes to apply: is the video the LCP element? Then it needs a **lightweight poster image** as the actual LCP paint, video attached after. What's the **file weight**? (This recording was ~16 Mbps — nowhere near shippable as-is.) Autoplay on cellular = data/battery, and **iOS Low Power Mode blocks autoplay entirely** → needs a fallback.
70	- Rule of thumb learned: *any* autoplay video hero is a perf story first and a motion story second.
71	
72	### b) Accessibility — WCAG 2.2 AA is the target, not a nice-to-have
73	- **`prefers-reduced-motion`** must have a defined behaviour for *every* animation. This is a first-class requirement to put in the story, not a dev afterthought.
74	- **Hover-only interactions fail on touch + keyboard** (WCAG 1.4.13). The tile carousel is hover-triggered → no defined behaviour on mobile/keyboard. This is both an a11y gap *and* the biggest scope gap.
75	- Icon-only controls need real `aria-label`s + visible focus (our `.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/` mechanically enforce `aria-label` on `IconButton`).
76	- Auto-playing audio > 3s needs a control (WCAG 1.4.2) → confirm muted-by-default.
77	
78	### c) Multi-region reality
79	- 8 storefronts / 11 locales. Never assume a design is global. Ask: does this masthead apply everywhere or AU-first? Is the content (hero film, banner copy, product row) CMS-driven (Contentful) or hard-coded?
80	
81	### d) Consent / Didomi
82	- If the video or anything on the page is **third-party**, it's consent-gated and **fails closed** — it cannot sit on the critical path. Confirm the hero is first-party/self-hosted.
83	
84	### e) Component & tier impact (scope the right reviews early)
85	- This touches **Tier 2 shared files**: `overrides/app/components/header/` (Global Shell, both squads) and `overrides/app/components/product-tile/` (Squad B owns, notify Squad A) — the hover carousel + price reveal is a real behavioural change to a shared component.
86	- Plus two **net-new** components: an announcement bar and a hero-video component.
87	- Lesson: naming the tiers/owners up front turns "a nice homepage" into a concrete coordination + review plan.
88	
89	### f) Buildability of the artefact itself
90	- **A rendered `.mov` is not a spec.** It shows *what*, never *how fast* or *how*. To build (and to write testable acceptance criteria) we need durations, easing curves, delays per animation — ideally a Figma prototype / motion tokens, not a video. Flagging this protects the estimate: you cannot size motion work from a render.
91	
92	---
93	
94	## 3. Lesson: separate "what it shows" from "what's missing" — the gaps are the review
95	
96	The most valuable output wasn't critiquing the animation; it was naming what the prototype *didn't* cover:
97	- **Mobile** — entirely absent, yet nearly every behaviour is hover/scroll-dependent.
98	- **States** — no paused / muted / autoplay-blocked / reduced-motion / slow-connection states.
99	- **Rest of page** — no footer, no full scroll (confirmed masthead-only).
100	
101	**Takeaway:** for any prototype, explicitly ask "what states and breakpoints are *not* here?" The absence is usually where the real work (and risk) hides.
102	
103	---
104	
105	## 4. Lesson: incorporate the whole team's signal, and weight it
106	
107	- **Bianca** raised two genuine gaps (banner sticky-when-open; can we pause). I verified the pause answer (yes) and confirmed the banner behaviour is a real hole — then *credited her* in the message so the questions read as a team, not a solo review.
108	- **Tim's one-liner** — "A carousel on every product on the PLP!" — is small but important: it extends the concern from the *homepage feature row* to **every tile on a PLP**, which multiplies the perf/bandwidth and visual-noise cost dozens of times over. A good lead treats a throwaway comment as a real requirements question ("is this pattern site-wide or homepage-only?") and folds it in rather than losing it in chat.
109	
110	**Takeaway:** synthesise all inputs into one coherent artefact and attribute them. It builds trust and stops the same question being asked three times.
111	
112	---
113	
114	## 5. Lesson: match the register of the audience, not the depth of your analysis
115	
116	I did a long, thorough internal review (perf, a11y, tiers, consent, regional). But the message that went out was **~7 plain bullets in Bianca's casual style**, because:
117	- The audience is a manager + an external motion designer, not engineers.
118	- The goal is *answers*, and people answer short, scannable, jargon-free questions.
119	- The rigour still lives in *me* (and in this log + the stories we'll write) — it doesn't need to be dumped on Jon.
120	
121	Also learned a small style point that matters to this stakeholder set: **no em-dashes**, plain sentence connectors. Little things signal you're writing *to them*.
122	
123	**Takeaway:** the analysis and the communication are two separate deliverables. Do the deep one for yourself; send the compressed one. Depth ≠ length.
124	
125	---
126	
127	## 6. Reusable checklist — "Reviewing a design/motion prototype" (keep this)
128	
129	1. **Verify** the artefact frame-by-frame; don't trust a single watch. Read the file metadata (size, dimensions, name) for scope clues.
130	2. **Inventory** exactly what it shows (behaviours + states).
131	3. **Name the gaps**: which breakpoints (esp. mobile), which states, which pages are missing?
132	4. **Pressure-test against the hard constraints:**
133	   - Performance (LCP ≤ 2s p75 mobile; autoplay video = poster + weight + fallback)
134	   - Accessibility (reduced-motion story, hover→touch/keyboard equivalent, aria-labels, audio control)
135	   - Multi-region (all sites vs AU-first; CMS-driven vs fixed)
136	   - Consent (first-party vs third-party / Didomi fail-closed)
137	   - Tier/ownership (which Tier 2 files, which squads, what net-new components)
138	   - Buildability (is there a motion spec / Figma, or just a render?)
139	5. **Fold in every teammate's signal** and attribute it.
140	6. **Don't estimate** until the must-have clarifications (motion spec, mobile, reduced-motion, region scope) are answered.
141	7. **Compress** to the audience's register. Deep review for you; short message for them.
142	
143	---
144	
145	## 7. Open threads / next steps for me
146	
147	- Do **not** size stories until Jon answers: motion spec, mobile behaviour, reduced-motion, region scope.
148	- When capturing stories, split by owner/tier/risk: *announcement bar* · *sticky header + logo* · *hero video (perf/poster/consent-critical)* · *product-tile hover + mobile*.
149	- The hero video is the perf-critical one — treat it as its own story with explicit LCP/poster/fallback acceptance criteria.
150	- Chase down whether the tile carousel is homepage-only or site-wide (Tim's point) before it silently becomes a PLP-wide commitment.
151	
152	---
153	
154	*Source material for this log: the `HomeMasthead.mov` frame analysis, Bianca's and Tim's comments, and the review mapped against `AGENTS.md` + `.claude/rules/` (performance, accessibility, protected files) on 2026-08-07.*

```swift
import AVFoundation; import AppKit; import Foundation
let asset = AVURLAsset(url: URL(fileURLWithPath: "/path/to/video.mov"))
let gen = AVAssetImageGenerator(asset: asset)
gen.appliesPreferredTrackTransform = true
gen.requestedTimeToleranceBefore = .zero   // exact frame, not nearest keyframe
gen.requestedTimeToleranceAfter  = .zero
let dur = CMTimeGetSeconds(asset.duration), interval = 1.7
var t = 0.0, i = 0
while t < dur {
    if let cg = try? gen.copyCGImage(at: CMTime(seconds: t, preferredTimescale: 600), actualTime: nil) {
        let rep = NSBitmapImageRep(cgImage: cg)
        let data = rep.representation(using: .jpeg, properties: [.compressionFactor: 0.7])!
        try? data.write(to: URL(fileURLWithPath: String(format: "frames/f%02d.jpg", i)))
    }
    i += 1; t += interval
}
```

- `mdls -name kMDItemDurationSeconds -name kMDItemPixelWidth -name kMDItemPixelHeight file.mov` gives you duration/resolution instantly with no tooling.

---

## 2. Lesson: the FED Lead lens = pressure-test the design against the project's *hard* constraints

Anyone can list what a prototype does. The value I add is mapping it against the non-negotiables in `AGENTS.md` and `.claude/rules/`. This is the reusable framework — run any new UI/motion design through these gates:

### a) Performance budget (the one that kills homepages)
- **Budget:** LCP ≤ 2s at p75 mobile (`AGENTS.md > Performance`). A full-bleed **autoplay hero video** is the textbook way to blow this.
- Reflexes to apply: is the video the LCP element? Then it needs a **lightweight poster image** as the actual LCP paint, video attached after. What's the **file weight**? (This recording was ~16 Mbps — nowhere near shippable as-is.) Autoplay on cellular = data/battery, and **iOS Low Power Mode blocks autoplay entirely** → needs a fallback.
- Rule of thumb learned: *any* autoplay video hero is a perf story first and a motion story second.

### b) Accessibility — WCAG 2.2 AA is the target, not a nice-to-have
- **`prefers-reduced-motion`** must have a defined behaviour for *every* animation. This is a first-class requirement to put in the story, not a dev afterthought.
- **Hover-only interactions fail on touch + keyboard** (WCAG 1.4.13). The tile carousel is hover-triggered → no defined behaviour on mobile/keyboard. This is both an a11y gap *and* the biggest scope gap.
- Icon-only controls need real `aria-label`s + visible focus (our `.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/` mechanically enforce `aria-label` on `IconButton`).
- Auto-playing audio > 3s needs a control (WCAG 1.4.2) → confirm muted-by-default.

### c) Multi-region reality
- 8 storefronts / 11 locales. Never assume a design is global. Ask: does this masthead apply everywhere or AU-first? Is the content (hero film, banner copy, product row) CMS-driven (Contentful) or hard-coded?

### d) Consent / Didomi
- If the video or anything on the page is **third-party**, it's consent-gated and **fails closed** — it cannot sit on the critical path. Confirm the hero is first-party/self-hosted.

### e) Component & tier impact (scope the right reviews early)
- This touches **Tier 2 shared files**: `overrides/app/components/header/` (Global Shell, both squads) and `overrides/app/components/product-tile/` (Squad B owns, notify Squad A) — the hover carousel + price reveal is a real behavioural change to a shared component.
- Plus two **net-new** components: an announcement bar and a hero-video component.
- Lesson: naming the tiers/owners up front turns "a nice homepage" into a concrete coordination + review plan.

### f) Buildability of the artefact itself
- **A rendered `.mov` is not a spec.** It shows *what*, never *how fast* or *how*. To build (and to write testable acceptance criteria) we need durations, easing curves, delays per animation — ideally a Figma prototype / motion tokens, not a video. Flagging this protects the estimate: you cannot size motion work from a render.

---

## 3. Lesson: separate "what it shows" from "what's missing" — the gaps are the review

The most valuable output wasn't critiquing the animation; it was naming what the prototype *didn't* cover:
- **Mobile** — entirely absent, yet nearly every behaviour is hover/scroll-dependent.
- **States** — no paused / muted / autoplay-blocked / reduced-motion / slow-connection states.
- **Rest of page** — no footer, no full scroll (confirmed masthead-only).

**Takeaway:** for any prototype, explicitly ask "what states and breakpoints are *not* here?" The absence is usually where the real work (and risk) hides.

---

## 4. Lesson: incorporate the whole team's signal, and weight it

- **Bianca** raised two genuine gaps (banner sticky-when-open; can we pause). I verified the pause answer (yes) and confirmed the banner behaviour is a real hole — then *credited her* in the message so the questions read as a team, not a solo review.
- **Tim's one-liner** — "A carousel on every product on the PLP!" — is small but important: it extends the concern from the *homepage feature row* to **every tile on a PLP**, which multiplies the perf/bandwidth and visual-noise cost dozens of times over. A good lead treats a throwaway comment as a real requirements question ("is this pattern site-wide or homepage-only?") and folds it in rather than losing it in chat.

**Takeaway:** synthesise all inputs into one coherent artefact and attribute them. It builds trust and stops the same question being asked three times.

---

## 5. Lesson: match the register of the audience, not the depth of your analysis

I did a long, thorough internal review (perf, a11y, tiers, consent, regional). But the message that went out was **~7 plain bullets in Bianca's casual style**, because:
- The audience is a manager + an external motion designer, not engineers.
- The goal is *answers*, and people answer short, scannable, jargon-free questions.
- The rigour still lives in *me* (and in this log + the stories we'll write) — it doesn't need to be dumped on Jon.

Also learned a small style point that matters to this stakeholder set: **no em-dashes**, plain sentence connectors. Little things signal you're writing *to them*.

**Takeaway:** the analysis and the communication are two separate deliverables. Do the deep one for yourself; send the compressed one. Depth ≠ length.

---

## 6. Reusable checklist — "Reviewing a design/motion prototype" (keep this)

1. **Verify** the artefact frame-by-frame; don't trust a single watch. Read the file metadata (size, dimensions, name) for scope clues.
2. **Inventory** exactly what it shows (behaviours + states).
3. **Name the gaps**: which breakpoints (esp. mobile), which states, which pages are missing?
4. **Pressure-test against the hard constraints:**
   - Performance (LCP ≤ 2s p75 mobile; autoplay video = poster + weight + fallback)
   - Accessibility (reduced-motion story, hover→touch/keyboard equivalent, aria-labels, audio control)
   - Multi-region (all sites vs AU-first; CMS-driven vs fixed)
   - Consent (first-party vs third-party / Didomi fail-closed)
   - Tier/ownership (which Tier 2 files, which squads, what net-new components)
   - Buildability (is there a motion spec / Figma, or just a render?)
5. **Fold in every teammate's signal** and attribute it.
6. **Don't estimate** until the must-have clarifications (motion spec, mobile, reduced-motion, region scope) are answered.
7. **Compress** to the audience's register. Deep review for you; short message for them.

---

## 7. Open threads / next steps for me

- Do **not** size stories until Jon answers: motion spec, mobile behaviour, reduced-motion, region scope.
- When capturing stories, split by owner/tier/risk: *announcement bar* · *sticky header + logo* · *hero video (perf/poster/consent-critical)* · *product-tile hover + mobile*.
- The hero video is the perf-critical one — treat it as its own story with explicit LCP/poster/fallback acceptance criteria.
- Chase down whether the tile carousel is homepage-only or site-wide (Tim's point) before it silently becomes a PLP-wide commitment.

---

*Source material for this log: the `HomeMasthead.mov` frame analysis, Bianca's and Tim's comments, and the review mapped against `AGENTS.md` + `.claude/rules/` (performance, accessibility, protected files) on 2026-08-07.*
